sections.label: Non-resident CPF accounts closing
sections.summary: CPF accounts of non-residents will be closed from 1 April 2024, as announced in March this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: First, we had earlier announced in March this year that CPF accounts of non-residents will be closed from 1 April 2024.

sections.label: Non-resident CPF transfer and interest
sections.summary: Non-residents should transfer CPF savings to bank accounts by 1 April 2024; monies in General Moneys earn 0.05% interest for three years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Non-residents should transfer their CPF savings to their bank accounts by 1 April 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: As a transitionary measure, in the first three years from 1 April 2024, non-residents' monies in the General Moneys of the Fund will earn interest based on the three-month average of the three local banks' savings account interest rate, which is currently at 0.05% per annum.

sections.label: Requests for deceased members' CPF information
sections.summary: This year CPF Board received over 3,000 requests to access deceased members' CPF information, often from family members.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Just this year alone, CPF Board has already received more than 3,000 requests to access deceased members' CPF information, often from their family members who are trying to settle the members' post-death matters.

sections.label: CPF Act Notice to Attend Court
sections.summary: The CPF Act will be amended to give CPF Board flexibility on the Notice to Attend Court form and document sending modes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Lastly, we will amend the CPF Act to allow CPF Board to have greater flexibility determining the form of the Notice to Attend Court for greater ease of administration and adopt more convenient and efficient modes of sending documents.

sections.label: Electronic service of CPF documents
sections.summary: The amendments will let CPF Board serve certain documents through an electronic service platform instead of hardcopy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The amendments will also allow CPF Board to serve certain documents through an electronic service platform instead of in hardcopy, as they are required to do so today.

sections.label: CPF Amendment Bill non-resident cessation
sections.summary: The CPF Amendment Bill ends non-residents' participation; foreigners must withdraw CPF monies or transfer them to General Moneys without interest from 1 April 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: The CPF Amendment Bill will effect the cessation of non-residents' participation in CPF schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: This will allow us to focus the CPF system on supporting the needs of residents who have a long-term commitment to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Following the amendment, foreigners who currently have CPF accounts will either have to withdraw all CPF monies standing to their credit or have their monies transferred to the General Moneys of the CPF Fund which would not bear interest on or after 1 April 2024.

sections.label: Unclaimed CPF monies and consent
sections.summary: Asks what percentage of deceased members' CPF accounts were not disbursed within a month, remained unclaimed after six months, and what percentage of members consented to post-death disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Since 2021, what percentage of deceased members' accounts was not disbursed and emptied within a month of the member's death being notified to CPF Board?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: And what percentage of deceased members' accounts still contained unclaimed CPF monies six months after CPF Board is notified of the member's death, such that the monies had to be transferred out into the general CPF fund and no further interest is payable on such monies?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Before these amendments, what percentage of CPF members gave their consent to the CPF Board to disclose information after death, when making their nominations of the persons entitled to receive their CPF monies upon their death?

sections.label: EP holders in Singapore
sections.summary: As of June 2023, Singapore has almost 200,000 EP holders, close to 6% of the labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, as of June 2023, there are almost 200,000 EP holders in Singapore, accounting for close to 6% of the labour force.

sections.label: EP versus Singaporean worker costs
sections.summary: A company can hire an EP holder at $5,000 monthly, while a Singaporean worker costs the employer $5,850 with CPF but takes home $4,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: A company can hire a foreign professional holding an EP at a monthly salary of $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But the employer would have to pay an extra $850 in CPF contributions for the Singaporean worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Singaporean's wage bill for the employer is $5,850, but the Singaporean only gets to take home $4,000.

sections.label: Average CPF interest rate
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng revealed the overall average CPF interest rate from 2018 to 2022 is close to 4% per annum, meaning less than 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In a written answer to my colleague Ms Hazel Poa's question in September, Minister Tan See Leng revealed that the overall average CPF interest rate, including extra interest, across the different types of CPF accounts and balances, from 2018 to 2022, is close to 4% per annum, which means it is less than 4% per annum.

sections.label: Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme implementation
sections.summary: The Government accepted the recommendation to set up the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme in 2016 but has not implemented it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government had accepted the recommendation to set up the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, it has still not yet been implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government should not stay silent on this issue and set up the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme so that Singaporeans have the option to increase the returns on their Ordinary Account and Special Account savings by investing them in low-fee, passively managed investment products.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If the Government is not prepared to allow Singaporeans to do this, then it should increase the interest rates that it pays to CPF members.

sections.label: Bill changes death notification timing
sections.summary: The Bill changes the relevant time from the actual time of death to the time CPF is notified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill changes this from the actual time of death to the time CPF is notified.

sections.label: Non-SC/PR CPF accounts remain
sections.summary: About 300,000 non-SC/PR individuals remain in the CPF system despite a ban on foreign contributions since 2003.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Despite the prohibition on contributions from foreigners since 2003, about 300,000 non-SC/PR individuals remain in the CPF system.

sections.label: Payouts when accounts close
sections.summary: It asks how much CPF expects to pay out when these accounts close and how much is accrued interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How much does CPF expect to pay out when these accounts are closed and how much of these payments are accrued interest?

sections.label: Beneficiaries without will or order
sections.summary: It asks what mechanisms ensure requestors are likely beneficiaries when a member dies without a will or Court order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What mechanisms will be in place to ensure that the requestors are likely beneficiaries when a member passes away without a will or Court order?

sections.label: Closing 300,000 non-SC/PR accounts
sections.summary: It asks the operational savings from closing about 300,000 non-SC/PR accounts set up before 2003, whose savings will cease earning CPF interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Much work and resources are required to administer CPF accounts and to pay interests on the funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is timely to close the roughly 300,000 accounts set up by non-SC/PRs from more than 20 years ago, before 2003.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How much operational savings is expected as a result of these amendments?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the closure of these accounts, the remaining savings will cease to earn the prevailing CPF interest rates.

sections.label: Next-of-kin not nominee or beneficiary
sections.summary: It asks what happens if the next-of-kin is neither a nominee nor beneficiary under amendments disclosing deceased members' CPF information without a Court order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Regarding the amendments to disclose deceased members' CPF information to nominees and beneficiaries without the need to obtain a Court order, what happens if the next-of-kin is neither a nominee nor beneficiary?

sections.label: Ceasing non-resident CPF participation
sections.summary: It states mandatory CPF contributions for non-residents were removed since 1995 and voluntary contributions disallowed since 2003.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Actually, we have been gradually moving towards ceasing the participation of non-residents in the CPF system across the years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We have removed mandatory CPF contributions for non-residents since 1995 and disallowed voluntary CPF contributions by non-residents since 2003.

sections.label: Non-residents' CPF balances
sections.summary: About 300,000 non-residents will cease CPF participation, and roughly 70% of them have less than S$5,000 in their CPF accounts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Yip Hon Weng and Mr Don Wee also asked about the size of CPF balances being transferred out of the CPF system.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: There are approximately 300,000 non-residents who will cease participation in the CPF schemes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The majority of these non-residents have low CPF balances, with approximately 70% of them having less than S$5,000 in their CPF accounts.

sections.label: Unclaimed non-resident CPF monies
sections.summary: There is no deadline for non-residents or their beneficiaries to claim CPF monies, which stay in the General Money of the Fund.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: He also asked what CPF Board would do with the unclaimed monies and whether it could be used, for example, as part of the Ministry of Manpower (MOM)'s budget.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: There is no deadline for non-residents to transfer their CPF monies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If non-residents have passed on, there is also no deadline for their nominees or beneficiaries under the relevant intestacy laws to claim the monies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: These unclaimed monies will continue to be held for the non-residents in the General Money of the Fund.

sections.label: CPF interest rate floors
sections.summary: Despite low interest rates since the global financial crisis, the Government paid CPF floor rates of 4% and 2.5%.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Despite the low interest rate environment in the last decade since the global financial crisis, the Government paid generous CPF interest rates due to the floor rates of 4% for the Special, MediSave and Retirement Accounts and 2.5% for the Ordinary Account.

sections.label: Deceased members' CPF disbursement
sections.summary: From 2021 to 2023, about 70% of deceased members' CPF monies were disbursed within five weeks, and children receive equal portions under the Intestate Succession Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: From 2021 to 2023, on average, around 70% of deceased members' CPF monies were disbursed by CPF Board or transferred to the Public Trustee for disbursement within five weeks upon notification of death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: For the same period, on average, only 5% of nominated monies remained unclaimed six months after notification of death.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Mr Don Wee asked whether in the event that the member and their spouse have passed on, would the children from the marriage be considered as next-of-kin and receive the same amount of CPF monies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Now, where the deceased member did not make a nomination for his CPF monies, the member's children would be considered next-of-kin and receive equal portions based on the distribution rules under the Intestate Succession Act.

sections.label: Qualifying Salary and repeated PQs
sections.summary: The minimum Qualifying Salary was only $3,900 until December 2020, and the question is irrelevant to today's CPF amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: In fact, I think until December 2020, the minimum Qualifying Salary was only $3,900.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This question that Mr Leong has asked has also been answered several times in the PQs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: It is irrelevant to today's amendment Bill and I think if he wants to really have even more PQs answered on this, he should file PQs in subsequent Sittings.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I do not want to waste Members' time arguing about something that has been answered before, that is irrelevant to today's administrative amendment of two particular aspects of the CPF.
